concepts.interpretation: The Court acknowledged the State's margin of appreciation in limiting the right of access to court but emphasized the right's essence must not be impaired.
The Court applied the proportionality test to assess whether the limitation pursued a legitimate aim and was proportionate.
The Court emphasized the positive obligation of authorities to allow effective judicial control even when national security is invoked.
The Court held that limitations must not impair the very essence of the right of access to court under Article 6 § 1.
The Court treats the right to a court under Article 6 § 1 as an autonomous concept requiring effective access and fairness.
The Court noted that sub-paragraphs of Article 6 § 3 apply in criminal matters but considered them as aspects of the general fairness guarantee.
